purpose: A second, separate content pillar alongside the B2B wholesale-buyer cluster plan (cluster-plan.json). Authorized by the site owner on 2026-09-15 as a deliberate strategy expansion: consumer-intent topics are now allowed where they can realistically bring organic traffic, but only after passing the same discipline the B2B plan already uses -- not written just because a keyword is trending.
audience_note: Consumer/individual-shopper intent, distinct from the wholesale-buyer ICP the main cluster-plan.json targets. Posts here should NOT push the wholesale ordering flow (WhatsApp/Telegram confirmation, 500-unit threshold mechanics) the way B2B posts do -- that CTA pattern belongs to Cluster 1-5 in cluster-plan.json, not here.
methodology: 1. Query must be genuinely perfume/fragrance/beauty related (checked against source data, not assumed).
2. Must have a real, verified catalog/product match -- checked directly against the live Supabase products/brands tables, not assumed from a brand name appearing in a trends export.
3. Current live SERP must be checked (WebSearch or equivalent) before any keyword is chosen -- who actually ranks, aggregator/big-box-dominated or independent-blog-winnable.
4. No invented search volume. Google Trends 'search interest' is a relative 0-100 index and % change figures are reported as-given, never treated as absolute volume.
5. No article gets written solely because a keyword is trending -- relevance + catalog match + winnable SERP all three must hold.

6. Structural rule: posts in this pillar link one-directionally (if at all) into the B2B wholesale content -- never mandatory bidirectional links, to avoid diluting the wholesale cluster's topical-authority signal documented in cluster-plan.json.
source_data: User-supplied Google Trends CSV exports (worldwide, 'perfume'-related top + rising queries, pulled 2026-09-14/15) -- see chat history for the raw files.

A Google Trends 'trending_US_4h' realtime export was also supplied and checked: zero perfume/fragrance/beauty relevance across all 40 rows (sports, celebrity news, politics, tech) -- excluded entirely, no queries extracted from it.

posts.catalog_match_note: IMPORTANT constraint discovered during research: Royal Perfumes' product data has NO 'inspired by [Designer X]' field or naming convention anywhere (checked products table directly + description_en text for the niche/inspired brand lines, e.g. Nishapur). The company's designer-branded catalog items (Dior, Chanel, etc.) are genuine wholesale-supplied originals, not dupes of themselves. The niche/inspired line (Nishapur, HFC, French Avenue, Morph, Gisada, Thomas Kosmala) markets under its own identity with no stated designer target. Therefore this post and any future posts in this pillar must NOT claim a specific Royal Perfumes SKU is 'a dupe for' a specific named designer perfume -- that would be an unverifiable, fabricated product claim. Content stays educational/general; ProductCallout usage (if any) must present a SKU as 'an example of a scent-matched fragrance,' never as a named-brand equivalence.
